data.title: Shift the event position in GaussSmearVertex and FlatSmearVertex so that beam particles are smeared too
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- `GaussSmearVertex`, `FlatSmearVertex`: shift the event position together with the vertices, so that beam particles start at the smeared interaction point instead of (0,0,0). Fixes #63.

ENDRELEASENOTES

The smearing tools shifted each vertex in `GenEvent::vertices()`. The beam particles come out of the HepMC3 root vertex, whose position is the event position. The root vertex is not in that list, so the beams stayed at (0,0,0) while everything else moved. `GenEvent::shift_position_by` shifts the event position and all vertices. Vertices without an explicit position take theirs from the (shifted) event position or their parent vertex, so they end up where they were before.

data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
-  HepMC3EventReader: apply the length unit to the primary vertex position

ENDRELEASENOTES

## Summary

Apply the HepMC3 event length unit when setting the primary vertex position in `HepMC3EventReader`.

The particle production/end positions are already converted using `len_unit`, and the vertex time is converted as well, but the `x`, `y`, and `z` coordinates of the corresponding `Geant4Vertex` were previously used without applying the HepMC3 length unit.

This is invisible for HepMC3 files using millimetres, but gives incorrect vertex positions for events using centimetres.

data.author: scott-snyder

PairCaloClustersPi0 tries to find all pairs of clusters with invariant mass consistent with the pi0 mass, subject to the constraint that no cluster is used by more than one pair.  It was doing this combinatoric problem by exhaustive search, which was exponential in both space and time. The combinatoric problem is, however, equivalent to that of finding a maximum matching of a graph (<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matching_(graph_theory)>). Boost.graph supplies an algorithm (Galil, https://doi.org/10.1145/6462.6502) that solves this in N^3 time (and i think linear space). Rewrite this algorithm to use this.

data.author: Jullianwatts

These commits are from @trholmes. I am submitting a PR because downstream
work depends on them.

Adds two energy correction plugins that look up a correction factor in a 2D

- HadronicThetaEnergyBinned, hadronic

nothing has to be applied by hand downstream.
